newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates barely changed in week.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates barely changed in week.

text.p: Home mortgage rates were barely changed this week amid signs that inflation remains under control, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgage rates were unchanged at 7.84 percent, while 15-year rates fell to 7.34 percent from 7.35 percent last week, the company said.
One-year adjustable mortgage rates inched up to 5.61 percent from 5.54 percent, it added.
A year ago, the 30-year loan rate averaged 7.83 percent, the 15-year 7.32 percent and the adjustable loan 5.55 percent.

"Since (Federal Reserve) Chairman (Alan) Greenspan's remarks pushed interest rates up two weeks ago, the economic news continues to point to a strong economy with no great threat of inflation," Freddie Mac chief economist Robert Van Order said.
"With these conditions in place, interest rates remain steady this week. Further, it appears these figures will stay stable through the coming week, at least," Van Order added.
In its Beige Book survey of U.S. economic conditions issued Wednesday, the Fed said that while job markets are tight, wage gains appear moderate and price pressures temperate.
Last week the Labour Department reported a U.S. February unemployment rate of 5.3 percent. On Friday the department will issue February producer prices.
Lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, and 1.4 percent on adjustable mortgages, all unchanged from last week.
Freddie Mac, formerly the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
